title: stapel brief: the builder brief of one step

confirmations.text:
Terms:

- **Brief command**: `stapel brief KEY STEP`.
- **Step item**: the Plan line whose label (`next::plan_steps`) is `step <STEP>`, and the lines after it up
  to the next step line, a blank line or the end of the Plan; ids are read in it with every run of
  whitespace (line breaks too) taken as one space, and it is printed as written.
- **Named criterion**: `AC-<n>` in the step item, and every `AC-<i>` with n ≤ i ≤ m for `AC-<n> to AC-<m>`.
- **Criterion row**: a Spec line that starts with `| AC-<n> |`; its tests are the backticked
  `<module>::<name>` names of its last cell.
- **Finding prefix**: the part of a finding id before its last `-<digits>` (`D1` of `D1-2`, `SR1` of
  `SR1-1`).
- **Named finding**: a word `<prefix>-<digits>` of the step item (not `AC`) whose prefix is the finding
  prefix of a record in the ticket's `findings.jsonl`; ranges as for a named criterion, with one prefix.
- **Term**: each `**<name>**:` of the list between the Spec line `Terms:` and the criteria table, with the
  text up to the next such name; a text uses it when `<name>` occurs in it as whole words, ASCII case
  ignored, the last word also with `s` or `es` added.
- **Step test**: when the step item holds backticked `<module>::<name>` names that a criterion row or the
  cases table names, exactly those, in step order; else a test of a named criterion, in Spec order; each once.
- **Names a test**: a cell holds a backticked name equal to the test; a test of the step is a step test.
- **Cases table**: the first table of the `## Test plan` section before its first `###` heading; **Inputs table** and **External states
  table**: the tables under `### Inputs` and `### External states` in it.
- **Estimated tokens**: the bytes of a text divided by 4, rounded up.

| № | Criterion | Test |
|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | WHEN the brief command runs on an open or closed ticket whose Plan has the step THE command prints the line `# Brief: <KEY> step <STEP>` (`<KEY>` the folder key, here and below), the header lines, then the parts of AC-3 to AC-9 in that order, each under its `## ` heading, leaving out a part with nothing in it; exit 0; it writes no file. Output: `golden/brief_text.txt`. | `brief::prints_the_brief`, `brief::writes_nothing`, `brief::closed_ticket`, `brief::runs_in_an_agent_shell`, `brief::lettered_step_and_folder_key`, `brief::missing_parts_of_the_ticket` |

| AC-3 | WHEN the Description has a `### Frame` subsection THE part `## Frame` holds its lines up to the next heading, without each paragraph that starts with `**Prior art.**` or `**Size.**`, trimmed. | `brief::frame_without_prior_art_and_size`, `brief::frame_edges` |
| AC-4 | WHEN the brief is printed THE part `## Step` holds the step item as written in the Plan. | `brief::prints_the_brief`, `brief::step_item_ends_at_a_blank_line` |
| AC-5 | WHEN the step item has a named criterion THE part `## Criteria` holds the header row and separator of the Spec criteria table, then each criterion row of a named criterion in Spec order, once. | `brief::criteria_and_ranges`, `brief::tests_from_the_last_cell`, `brief::header_of_the_criteria_table` |
| AC-6 | WHEN a printed criterion row (not the header row or separator) uses a term THE part `## Terms` holds that term and each term a printed term uses, until none is added, in Spec order, once; a line shared by two terms is printed once, and each term on it counts as printed, also along a chain of shared lines. | `brief::terms_used_and_their_terms`, `brief::terms_list_ends_at_the_table`, `brief::terms_from_the_rows_only`, `brief::terms_on_a_shared_line`, `brief::terms_on_a_chain_of_lines`, `brief::term_text_ends_at_the_next_name`, `brief::term_text_ends_on_its_own_line` |
| AC-7 | WHEN a row of the cases table names a test of the step, or its first cell holds `step <STEP>` as whole words, THE part `## Cases` holds the header row, separator and each such row. | `brief::cases_of_the_step`, `brief::cases_table_before_the_subsections`, `brief::cases_of_a_step_without_criteria` |
| AC-8 | WHEN the last cell of a row of the Inputs table or the External states table names a test of the step THE parts `## Inputs` and `## External states` hold the header row, separator and each such row of their table. | `brief::rows_of_the_step_tests` |
| AC-9 | WHEN the step item has a named finding THE part `## Findings` holds one line per named finding in step order, once: `- <id> (<severity>): <claim> Fate: <fate>`, from the last well-formed record with that id, `none` for a missing field or one that is not a string, every run of whitespace in a field printed as one space. | `brief::findings_last_record`, `brief::finding_fields_on_one_line`, `brief::finding_prefixes_exact`, `brief::finding_fields_not_strings`, `brief::no_findings_file` |
| AC-10 | IF `STEP` is not digits followed by at most one lowercase letter, or `KEY` names no ticket or several in case, THEN the command prints `stapel: <reason>` on stderr and exits 2; IF the ticket is legacy, or `ticket.md`, `state.json` or an existing `findings.jsonl` cannot be read as a whole, THEN it exits 1 with `stapel: <reason>`. | `brief::refuses_a_wrong_call`, `brief::refuses_an_unreadable_ticket` |
| AC-11 | IF the Plan has no step `step <STEP>`, or no `plan` section is configured, THEN the command prints `stapel: the Plan of <KEY> has no step <STEP>` and exits 1; IF it has the step twice THEN `stapel: the Plan of <KEY> names step <STEP> twice`, exit 1. | `brief::step_not_in_the_plan` |
| AC-12 | IF a named criterion has no criterion row THEN the command prints `stapel: step <STEP> names AC-<n>, which the Spec does not have`, and IF a range has n > m THEN `stapel: step <STEP> names AC-<n> to AC-<m>, which is not a range`, for the first such id or range in step order; exit 1. | `brief::unknown_criterion`, `brief::unknown_ids_in_step_order`, `brief::refusals_in_step_order` |
| AC-13 | IF a named finding has no well-formed record THEN the command prints `stapel: step <STEP> names <id>, which findings.jsonl does not have` for the first such id, and IF a finding range has n > m THEN `stapel: step <STEP> names <id> to <id>, which is not a range`, for the first in step order; exit 1. | `brief::unknown_finding`, `brief::finding_range_not_a_range` |
| AC-14 | IF the step item has no named criterion and no named finding THEN the command prints `stapel: step <STEP> names no criterion and no finding` and exits 1. | `brief::step_names_nothing` |
| AC-15 | IF the brief has more than 1600 estimated tokens THEN stdout is empty, the command prints `stapel: the brief of step <STEP> has <n> tokens, more than 1600: <part> <n>, …` (header and every printed part, in print order, each rounded up on its own, so they may sum to more than the total) and exits 1. | `brief::too_large`, `brief::size_counts_bytes` |
| AC-16 | WHEN `stapel next` names `build-step` or `green-step` for a label that is a Plan step and its brief assembles THE target is the command `stapel brief <KEY> <STEP>` (text after ` — `; `command` in `--json`, `path` `null`); without a `plan` section it stays the ticket path. | `next::build_step_names_the_brief` |
| AC-17 | IF that brief refuses with exit 1 (AC-11 to AC-15) THEN `stapel next` adds the fact `brief of step <STEP>: <the refusal without stapel: >` and the action line is `next: write-section <title of the plan section> — <ticket path>`; exit 0; an existing `findings.jsonl` that cannot be read as a whole exits 1, as `next` did before. | `next::brief_refusal_blocks_the_step`, `next::brief_refusal_names_sizes_and_title`, `next::unreadable_findings_file` |
| AC-18 | WHEN the step has a step test THE header ends with the line `tests: <each step test, joined by ", ">`; with none the line is left out. | `brief::prints_the_brief`, `brief::empty_parts_are_left_out`, `brief::explicit_step_tests`, `brief::explicit_tests_are_known_tests` |

### Guarantees

- **Promised:** the Frame's promise, by AC-1 to AC-18; the guard lets the brief command run in an agent's
  shell; `stapel next` keeps every other action and target for a step whose brief assembles; in `--json`,
  `path` is `null` for a `build-step` or `green-step` that names the brief; the facts of `next` (AC-1 of
  STP-20) gain the kind `brief of step <STEP>: …`, so a step of an open ticket that names no criterion and
  no finding now stops `next` (AC-14, AC-17).
- **Not promised:** the Frame's list; a Terms list in another form than `- **<name>**:` items (D10-1); a criterion that refers to other criteria by id (they are not pulled in; E-2); a `**<name>**:` inside inline code in the Terms list counts as a term (E-3); a typo in a finding prefix (`DX-1`); leading zeros (`AC-01` reads as `AC-1`); a Spec with two tables of criterion rows, or a criteria table without a separator (D3D-1, D3D-2); other range forms (`AC-3–AC-5`,
  `AC-3..AC-5`, `AC-3 to 5`); an exclusion in the step (`AC-1 without <test>`: every test of AC-1 is a step
  test); other inflections of a term (`criteria` for `criterion`, `is done` for `Done step`); a term or step
  line inside a code fence; a Frame paragraph that starts `**Prior art**` without the dot; ids in other
  sections than the step item.

### Facts

- F-1: `tickets::resolve` gives the ticket choice and its texts; `stapel next` maps them to exit 2 and a
  legacy or unreadable ticket to exit 1 (STP-20, `crates/stapel-cli/src/next.rs`).
- F-2: `next::plan_steps` and `step_label` give the labels of the Plan (`step 1c`), repeats kept;
  `ticket::parse` and `ticket::find` give `## ` sections, so `### Frame`, `### Inputs` and `### External
  states` are found inside the body of their section.
- F-3: the guard treats only `ok`, `close`, `findings` and `ledger` of `stapel` as person commands
  (`guard::check_stapel`); every other subcommand passes.
- F-4: `next::history_action` builds `build-step` and `green-step` with `Target::Path(ticket_path)`.

### Decisions (before the build)

- A pure function `stapel_core::brief::assemble` takes the ticket text, the `findings.jsonl` text, the key,
  the step and the base, and returns the parts or a refusal; `crates/stapel-cli/src/brief.rs` reads the
  files and prints. Most cases are tested through the binary on fixture tickets.
- The size check runs on the assembled text before anything is printed, so a refusal leaves stdout empty.
- `next` calls `assemble` only for the step it names, so its other actions read nothing new; it builds the
  brief command only when the label is a Plan step, so the no-`plan` case of AC-21 of STP-20 keeps its path.

### Decisions (as built)

- `stapel_core::brief::assemble(text, key, step, base, plan_title, findings)` is pure; a missing `plan`
  section is refused in the CLI as `has no step`; `crates/stapel-cli/src/brief.rs`
  checks `STEP` before it opens the repository (a bad `STEP` wins over a bad `KEY`), reads `findings.jsonl`
  (missing: `""`; any other read error: exit 1, `stapel: cannot read <path>: <err>`) and prints.
- Layout: each part is a blank line, `## <part>` and its text, with no blank line after the heading.
- Frame: the Description section (fixed title, as in `next`), from a `Frame` heading of any level to the
  next ATX heading; an empty Frame after the drop is left out.
- Criteria: named items are checked in step order, so the first bad range or unknown id is reported; the
  header row and separator come from the `|` block above the first criterion row (walked upward); tests
  are the backticked names with `::` in the last cell.
- Terms: read between `Terms:` and the first `|` line; matched only against criterion rows; a word is
  ASCII alphanumerics and `_`; a term prints as its Spec lines from its name to the line before the next
  name, and also that line when text comes before the next name on it; every term whose lines overlap a
  printed term counts as printed, followed to a fixed point (step 10, D4D-1).
- Step tests: the backticked `<module>::<name>` names of the step item when it has any, else the tests of
  the named criteria (step 10).
- Cases, Inputs, External states: the first `|` block of the Test plan section before its first heading;
  the first table under each `###` heading; also printed for a step without criteria.
- Findings: `findings_part` is built before any output; ranges expand lazily, and a reversed range
  refuses in step order; each field prints with whitespace runs as one space, a non-string field as
  `none`; `names_a_finding` keeps its own record parsing. `next` gives an unreadable `findings.jsonl` as
  `stapel: <path>: <os error>`, exit 1.
- Size: `MAX_TOKENS` 1600, `estimated_tokens` = `bytes.div_ceil(4)`; the parts split the brief's bytes
  with no rest, each rounded up on its own.
- `next`: `History` carries `brief: Option<(label, Option<refusal>)>`; the CLI decides, assembles the
  brief of the step the decision names when a `plan` section is configured, and decides again;
  `step_action` gives the brief command, or the fact and `write-section` on a refusal.
- Build notes: steps 3 and 8 had their RED rewritten with the human, because a test changed in a RED
  passed there (`no-red`; in step 8 only `rustfmt` reflow of an untouched test). Builders broke the
  Edit-or-Write rule four times (`cat >>`, `sed -i`); the guard does not deny it yet (item 1.9). The first
  use of the command on this ticket refused step 3 (1653 tokens) after a script had estimated 1348.

Route: full (tag `interface`), auto.

1. The command prints the header without its `tests:` line, the Frame and the Step (AC-1 to AC-4). Must not change: `stapel next`,
   `stapel status`, `ticket::parse`, `tickets::resolve`.
1c. Coverage after the drift review of step 1 (D1-1, D1-2, D1-3, D1-7): four new `#[test]` functions
   (`brief::lettered_step_and_folder_key`, `brief::base_of_state_json`,
   `brief::step_item_ends_at_a_blank_line`, `brief::frame_edges`) and `brief::step_not_in_the_plan` and
   `brief::refuses_an_unreadable_ticket` of AC-10 and AC-11, whose code step 1 already built. Tests only,
   each helper nested inside its function.
2. The check of `STEP` and the ticket choice (AC-10, test `brief::refuses_a_wrong_call` only). Must not
   change: the brief of step 1 and the refusals tested in step 1c.
3. Criteria, the `tests:` line and the unknown criterion (AC-5, AC-12, AC-18; the golden file holds the
   `tests:` line). Must not change: the parts of step 1.
3c. Coverage after the drift review of step 3 (D3-2, D3-5): two new `#[test]` functions
   (`brief::tests_from_the_last_cell`, `brief::unknown_ids_in_step_order`). Tests only, each helper nested
   inside its function.
3d. Fixes after the drift review of step 3 (D3-1, D3-3, D3-4): the header of the table that holds the
   criterion rows, and refusals in step order (AC-5, AC-12; tests `brief::header_of_the_criteria_table`,
   `brief::refusals_in_step_order` only). Must not change: the parts and refusals tested in steps 1 to 3c.
4. Terms and a step naming nothing (AC-6, AC-14). Must not change: the parts of steps 1 and 3.
4c. Coverage after the drift review of step 4 (D4-3): one new `#[test]` function
   (`brief::terms_list_ends_at_the_table`). Tests only, its helpers nested inside it.
4d. Fixes after the drift review of step 4 (D4-1, D4-2): terms from the criterion rows only, and a shared
   term line (AC-6; tests `brief::terms_from_the_rows_only`, `brief::terms_on_a_shared_line` only). Must
   not change: the parts and refusals tested in steps 1 to 4c.
5. Cases, Inputs and External states rows (AC-7, AC-8). Must not change: the parts of steps 1, 3 and 4.
6. Findings and the unknown finding (AC-9, AC-13), with `brief::empty_parts_are_left_out` of AC-18 (it
   needs the Findings part) and the `findings.jsonl` cases of `brief::refuses_an_unreadable_ticket`. Must not change: the format of `findings.jsonl` and
   `stapel findings`.
7. The size limit (AC-15). Must not change: the text of a brief within the limit.
8. `stapel next` names the brief and blocks on its refusal (AC-16, AC-17). The RED gives the shared
   fixtures of `tests/next.rs` (`written`, `ready` and the Plans `1. One.`) a criterion row `AC-1` and steps
   that name it, and changes the expected `build-step` and `green-step` targets. Must not change: every
   other action of `next`, its facts for a step whose brief assembles, and its exit codes.
9. Coverage after code review round 1 (D4D-2, D5-2, D6-1, D6-2, D6-3, D7-1, D8-1, D8-2, DR-3): new `#[test]`
   functions `brief::term_text_ends_at_the_next_name`, `brief::cases_of_a_step_without_criteria`,
   `brief::no_findings_file`, `brief::finding_prefixes_exact`, `brief::finding_fields_not_strings`,
   `brief::size_counts_bytes`, `brief::missing_parts_of_the_ticket`, `next::unreadable_findings_file`,
   `next::brief_refusal_names_sizes_and_title`. Tests only, helpers nested; a test that fails goes to step 10.
10. Fixes after code review round 1 (D4D-1, D5-1, D6-4, R-1, E-1): tests
   `brief::explicit_step_tests`, `brief::finding_range_not_a_range`, `brief::finding_fields_on_one_line`,
   `brief::cases_table_before_the_subsections`, `brief::terms_on_a_chain_of_lines`. Must not change: the
   briefs and refusals of steps 1 to 9 for a step whose text names no backticked test, except where (b) to

11. Fix after the drift review of step 10 (D10-2): a backticked name is a step test only when a criterion row or
   the cases table names it (test `brief::explicit_tests_are_known_tests`); the GREEN also corrects the
